text:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal to add a per-route SLA-aware soft-throttle that combines an abuse score and SLA weight to decide degrade vs reject. Thinking this sits as an admission layer before token accounting.
kevin: Can you sketch the decision boundary? soft-throttle = degrade probabilistically or route to fallback model?
maria: Exactly. high abuse -> hard reject. mid abuse && low SLA weight -> probabilistic degrade (lower-cost model or truncate). high SLA weight -> prefer queued delay or denser batching to keep quality.
elaine: Telemetry needs: tag events with route_sla_weight, abuse_score, chosen_action, fallback_model, latency_impact. otherwise we can't correlate regressions.
sahil: How do we compute abuse_score? streaming pattern detection? recent requests per-second + prompt reuse + token-entropy heuristic. ML-ish signal + rules.
maria: Agree — keep a deterministic rule-based baseline and an optional ML signal that gets gated behind human review. no ML decisions in the hot path until we can audit.
kevin: Interface boundary question: should admission live in edge proxies (local sidecar) or a central admission service? tradeoffs: local = low latency, can act on client hints; central = global view for accurate abuse scoring.
elaine: My vote: hybrid. sidecar enforces simple deterministic checks (rate windows, token caps, client-hint) and emits events. central admission applies scored decisions when it has enough global context and can orchestrate model fallback.
maria: Hybrid makes sense. sidecars fast-path, central for opaque heuristics. Also need clear fallbacks: model downgrade vs token trimming vs 429. Prefer degrade before outright reject for mid-tier customers.
sahil: For ML signal rollout: expose a "score_debug" in traces and a dry-run mode where central returns a suggested action but sidecar ignores it. Use that to build precision/recall.
kevin: Ops concern: failure modes. If central admission is unavailable, sidecar should default to permissive or conservative? We need an SLO-aligned default.
aria: (typo) maria: Default to permissive for high-SLA tenants, conservative for free/unknown tenants. documentable policy.
elaine: We also need a backoff policy for clients who trigger repeated mid-tier degradations — avoid oscillation. exponential backoff with decaying penalty score.
sahil: Suggest a small state machine per client id: OK -> prob-degrade -> hard-degrade -> probation -> OK. penalties decay over N minutes.
kevin: How does billing interact? If we downgrade to smaller model, do we bill full tokens or scaled? product question.
maria: Product needs to decide. My ops preference: bill actual resources consumed. But show transparency in console: "downgraded due to fairness policy". customers can opt-out with reserved capacity.
elaine: Security note: abuse_score must be auditable and reversible. add immutable event logs with inputs that contributed to score (hashed).
sahil: Implementation sketch: sidecar (rust) exposes /admit which returns immediate allow/deny or suggested_action. central admission service (python/Go) computes abuse_score by joining tenant telemetry + historical probes.
maria: Quick config example (proto config):
```
route: /v1/generate
soft_threshold: 0.7
decision_decay_minutes: 15
fallback_models: ["redwood-lean-v1", "redwood-std-quant"]
abuse_signal_window_s: 60
```
kevin: Nice. We'll need integration tests with synthetic probe clients and ramped ML signal to validate false-positive rates.
elaine: Observability: add a per-route HUD showing degrade rate, false-positive alert when degrade correlates with low abuse_score but high customer complaints.
sahil: Also add a simulation pipeline: replay historical traffic through new admission logic in dry-run and compute predicted revenue/latency delta.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy of central-admission v0.6 scheduled to infra/canary at 10:30am PT :white_check_mark:
maria: I'll open an RFC patch with the hybrid architecture, default policy, and rollout plan + acceptance criteria (dry-run FPR < 1% across top 50 tenants).
kevin: Tag me for interface review. I'll add API shape and error codes.
elaine: I'll own telemetry and alerting hooks.
sahil: I'll prototype the ML signals and the probation state machine.
maria: Thanks team — sync tomorrow 11am to align on rollout timeline.
